title: Algebraic-closure internal Hom comparison from finite-field continuity
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, let $E\subseteq\Omega$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $X$ be a scheme. Put $S=p_X^*\underline E$ and $T=p_X^*\underline\Omega$ on the small pro-étale site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the module universe and small-site convention [def-weil-size-convention], the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves and ambient relative internal Hom and tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For $M\in D(S)$ write $M_\Omega=T\otimes_S^L M$. Suppose $K\in D(S)$ has the following internal-sheaf continuity property: for every small filtered diagram $(M_i^\bullet)$ of $S$-module complexes with one common termwise lower bound, the evaluation comparison $\varinjlim_i R\mathcal Hom_S(K,M_i^\bullet)\to R\mathcal Hom_S(K,\varinjlim_iM_i^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism. Colimits here are exact termwise sheaf-module colimits of functorial representatives [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $L\in D(S)$ be bounded below in cohomology.

The canonical evaluation-transpose comparison
$$T\otimes_S^L R\mathcal Hom_S(K,L)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_T(K_\Omega,L_\Omega)$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K,L$. Specifically, finite intermediate fields $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$ form a small filtered cofinal subposet of the finite subextensions of $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$; their coefficient sheaves $F_X$ are finite free over $S$, and their sheaf-algebra colimit is $T$. After restriction to $D(S)$, the displayed map is the composite
$$T\otimes_S^L R\mathcal Hom_S(K,L)\simeq\varinjlim_F(F_X\otimes_S R\mathcal Hom_S(K,L))\simeq\varinjlim_F R\mathcal Hom_S(K,F_X\otimes_SL)\simeq R\mathcal Hom_S(K,T\otimes_SL).$$
The stage maps are induced by evaluation, commute with all field-inclusion transitions, and are independent of choices of finite bases. No constructibility, site-perfectness or completeness of $K,L$ is assumed beyond the displayed continuity and lower-bound hypotheses.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the poset of finite intermediate fields of $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $I_E$ its full subposet on fields containing $E$. These are small in the stipulated coefficient universe: an intermediate field is a subfield of the fixed set $\Omega$, hence these collections are sets there. The finite-compositum statement gives $FG\in I_E$ for $F,G\in I_E$, while $E\in I_E$. Thus $I_E$ is nonempty and filtered. For $H\in I$, $EH$ is finite and contains both $E$ and $H$. More explicitly, the poset of objects of $I_E$ above $H$ contains $EH$ and is directed by composita. Hence the inclusion $I_E\subseteq I$ is cofinal. These assertions require no condition on $X$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(2), finite-subextension index; explicit finite-compositum and smallness verification.

proof.text: For $F\in I_E$ put $A_F=F_X$ with its $S=E_X$-algebra structure induced by inclusion. For $F\ne E$, the finite-free coefficient lemma gives $A_F\cong S^{\oplus[F:E]}$; for $F=E$ use the identity $S\cong S^{\oplus1}$. This only chooses bases to verify the finite-free hypothesis. It does not define any comparison map using those bases. All coefficient transitions and cocone legs are the maps induced by the actual field inclusions.

source.place: Assertion (2), finite-free coefficient sheaves; identity extension treated separately.

proof.text: Write $a_{H,J}:H_X\to J_X$ for an inclusion and $q_H:H_X\to T$ for the closure coefficient map. The coefficient-composition lemma gives $q_Ja_{H,J}=q_H$; the maps $a$ themselves compose as their field inclusions do. The full ring-sheaf colimit is $T$ by the coefficient-colimit theorem. Its restriction to $I_E$ has the same universal property: given a ring-sheaf cocone $t_F:F_X\to B$ on $I_E$, extend it to $I$ by $\widetilde t_H=t_{EH}a_{H,EH}$. If $H\subseteq J$, then $EH\subseteq EJ$ and the cocone equation gives $\widetilde t_Ja_{H,J}=\widetilde t_H$. The full colimit therefore gives a unique $t:T\to B$. For $F\in I_E$, $EF=F$, so $tq_F=t_F$; conversely these equations force $tq_H=t_{EH}a_{H,EH}$ for every $H$, proving uniqueness. Thus the ring-sheaf colimit of the tail is $T$ with the specified $q_F$. For an $S$-algebra cocone, $tq_E=t_E$ is its structural map from $S$; the same universal map is therefore $S$-linear and gives the $S$-algebra colimit. The tail-module-colimit lemma supplies the underlying $S$-module colimit with these very same maps and actions. In particular $q_Fa_{E,F}=q_E$, as needed for a diagram of $S$-algebras.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(2); explicit restriction of its coefficient-ring colimit to F containing E, followed by the existing tail module comparison.

proof.text: Filtered colimits of $S$-module sheaves are exact on the chosen small site. Indeed, forget a small filtered diagram of short exact sequences to abelian sheaves. The module forgetful functor is exact and preserves its colimit, and filtered colimits of abelian sheaves are exact. It is faithful, so the vanishing of the underlying kernel/image quotient implies its vanishing as a module sheaf; it therefore reflects exactness as well. This proves the required exactness for precisely the small filtered index $I_E$. These are sheaf colimits, rather than an assertion that arbitrary section functors preserve colimits.

Transport to ringed-site module sheaves. The item's $D(S)$, $D(T)$, $\otimes^{\mathrm L}$ and $R\mathcal Hom$ are those of module objects over the ring objects $S=E_X$ and $T=\Omega_X$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], while the general comparison of step 6 is stated for sheaves of modules over a sheaf of rings, its K-flat tensor and the K-injective model $H_R$. Apply the module-object/ringed-site comparison to $B=S$ and to $B=T$: the equivalence $F$ leaves underlying abelian sheaves, sections and maps unchanged, its termwise extension $D(F)$ identifies the K-flat relative tensor with the ringed-site one (the tensor comparison: $F$ is exact, matches total tensor complexes and preserves and reflects K-flat complexes, so $T\otimes^{\mathrm L}_S-$ goes to derived scalar extension along the section-ring map $S_{\mathrm{sec}}\to T_{\mathrm{sec}}$), and gives isomorphisms $D(F)R\mathcal Hom_B(K,N)\cong H_{B_{\mathrm{sec}}}(D(F)K,D(F)N)$, natural in both variables and carrying evaluation to evaluation. Hence: (a) the finite-free and colimit statements of steps 2-3 hold verbatim for the section-ring sheaves, since $F$ does not change underlying sheaves or maps; (b) termwise colimits of complexes are unchanged by $D(F)$, and naturality in $N$ carries the evaluation-induced continuity map of the hypothesis on $K$ to the evaluation-induced map $\varinjlim_iH(D(F)K,M_i^\bullet)\to H(D(F)K,\varinjlim_iM_i^\bullet)$, which is therefore an isomorphism; (c) since the evaluation-transpose comparison is defined from evaluation morphisms and the scalar adjunction, the comparison of step 6 for $D(F)K,D(F)L$ corresponds under these isomorphisms to the item's displayed map, and likewise each stage map of the three-arrow formula. The lower bound of $L$ is unchanged.

proof.text: After the transport of step 5, apply the general filtered finite-free internal-Hom comparison to $D(F)K$ and $D(F)L$, with its base ring $R=S=E_X$, coefficient diagram $(S_i)=(A_F)_{F\in I_E}$, and colimit algebra equal to our $T$. Step 1 verifies a small filtered index, step 2 verifies finite freeness, step 3 verifies both the algebra and underlying module colimits with their given legs, and step 4 verifies exact filtered colimits. The hypothesis on $K$ applies to every small filtered diagram, hence to this particular index; the required lower-bound hypothesis on $L$ is exactly the one assumed here. The general theorem gives the canonical evaluation-transpose isomorphism in $D(T)$ (transported back by step 5), natural in both inputs, and identifies its restriction with the three-arrow formula in the statement. Its formula uses a bounded-below representative of $L$; no bound on a representative of $R\mathcal Hom_S(K,L)$ is required. The same theorem states that the finite-stage comparisons are induced by evaluation, commute with every transition of the algebra diagram, and are independent of finite bases. They give all the remaining clauses for our field diagram. No constructibility, completeness or site-perfectness hypothesis has entered this specialization.
